campbell.title: Campbell City Council — October 6, 2026
campbell.summary: The Campbell City Council's October 6, 2026 agenda includes a proclamation for Breast Cancer Awareness Month, routine approvals like bill payments and monthly financial reports, and several bigger items including a major grant application, staff compensation changes, and a city manager salary adjustment. The agenda also lists appointments to two city advisory bodies.
keyTopics: Proclamation recognizing October 2026 as Breast Cancer Awareness Month, honoring El Camino Health's breast cancer care services
Resolution authorizing an $8.5 million grant application to the California Department of Parks and Recreation's Statewide Park Development and Community Revitalization Program
Resolutions amending compensation and working conditions for unrepresented Confidential, Classified Management, and Unclassified Management employees
Resolution adjusting the City Manager's salary with a market adjustment
Appointments to the Bicycle and Pedestrian Advisory Committee and the Civic Improvement Commission

saratoga.title: Saratoga City Council — October 7, 2026
saratoga.summary: The Saratoga City Council's agenda for October 7, 2026 included routine items like meeting minutes and financial reports, along with several notable decisions: a $2.5 million budget amendment for the Hakone Gardens Koi Pond renovation, a new no-parking zone on Chester Avenue, and a major discussion on whether to switch the city's long-term law enforcement provider to the Los Gatos Monte Sereno Police Department. The agenda also listed a review of animal care service providers and a public hearing on annual updates to the City Code covering commissioner qualifications and appeal procedures.
keyTopics: Hakone Gardens Koi Pond Renovation budget amendment of $2,500,000
Decision on switching long-term law enforcement services to Los Gatos Monte Sereno Police Department
No Parking Anytime zone proposed for Chester Avenue near Arcadia Palms Drive
Comparison of animal care service providers, including continuing with San Jose Animal Care and Services
Annual Code Update public hearing on commissioner qualifications and appeal scheduling procedures

los-altos.title: Los Altos City Council — September 22, 2026
los-altos.summary: The Los Altos City Council agenda for September 22, 2026 included a wastewater treatment plant agreement, a Valley Transportation Authority board reappointment, a temporary moratorium on certain detention/custodial facility applications, and appointments to several city commissions. The agenda also listed a legal services contract amendment and a housing element implementation schedule for discussion.
keyTopics: Addendum No. 14 to the Regional Water Quality Control Plant Basic Agreement with Palo Alto and Mountain View
Reappointment of Councilmember Jonathan D. Weinberg to the VTA Board for an additional two years
Interim urgency ordinance establishing a temporary moratorium on applications for detention or custodial facilities and custodial-processing facilities
Appointments to the Complete Streets, Environmental, and Planning Commissions
Amendment No. 1 to the legal services agreement with Berliner Cohen, LLP, updating the monthly retainer to $21,500 for up to 70 hours and setting an hourly rate of $385

los-gatos.title: Los Gatos Town Council — October 6, 2026
los-gatos.summary: The Los Gatos Town Council's agenda for October 6, 2026, included routine approvals such as meeting minutes, accounts payable, and payroll reports. It also listed a bid issue with a tree services contractor, an amendment to an existing agreement, updates to the Finance Commission's work plan, a proposed change to the Town's purchasing policy, and a financial report covering July 2026 revenues and expenditures.
keyTopics: Relieving Denali Tree Services of its bid due to a bidder's mistake
First Amendment to an existing agreement authorized for execution by the Town Manager
Finance Commission's updated 2026 Work Plan
Resolution amending the Town's Purchasing Policy (Policy 4-06)
July 2026 Expenditure and Revenue Reports

san-jose.body: Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole
san-jose.title: San José Rules and Open Government Committee and Committee of the Whole — October 7, 2026
san-jose.summary: This is the agenda for San José's Rules and Open Government Committee meeting. The October 13, 2026 meeting was cancelled, and the body planned to review the draft agenda for October 20, 2026. Other listed items include routine reports, a proclamation request, and a discussion item on self-checkout safety standards at grocery and drug stores.
keyTopics: Review and planning of the October 20, 2026 draft agenda, including adding items and assigning time-certain slots
Public Record covering September 24 - October 1, 2026
Joint City of San José and Santa Clara Valley Water District Special Meeting
Proclamation, flag raising, and lighting recognizing Taiwan Retrocession Day, sponsored by Council District 5
Self-Checkout Safety Standards for Grocery and Drug Retail Stores, proposed by Council Members Candelas and Cohen

mountain-view.title: Mountain View Council Sustainability Committee — September 29, 2026
mountain-view.summary: This Mountain View Council Sustainability Committee agenda covers the city's draft Five-Year Community Decarbonization Plan and the 2024 Community Greenhouse Gas Emissions Inventory. It also includes standard opportunities for public comment and committee/staff discussion.
keyTopics: Draft Five-Year Community Decarbonization Plan
2024 Community Greenhouse Gas Emissions Inventory

sunnyvale.title: Sunnyvale City Council — October 6, 2026
sunnyvale.summary: The Sunnyvale City Council agenda for October 6, 2026 includes several recognitions (Little League All-Stars, Indigenous Peoples' Day, Friends of the Library Week, and Sunnyvale Stands United Against Hate Week), routine approvals, and two public hearings on water conservation rules and worker retention policy. The agenda also lists approval of public art for the Lakewood Park renovation and informational reports on pesticide elimination, artificial turf policy, and a potential linear park on PG&E-owned lots.
keyTopics: Public hearing to amend municipal code implementing AB 1572, prohibiting potable water use to irrigate nonfunctional turf (CEQA exempt under Guidelines Section 15307)
Discussion and possible action to introduce a Service Worker Retention Ordinance
Approval of public art for the Lakewood Park renovation
Amendment to extend and increase funding ($385,000 total) for environmental consulting services at the SMaRT Station and Sunnyvale Landfill

Informational reports on completed projects: eliminating chemical pesticide use on city property, an artificial turf policy study, and feasibility of a linear park on PG&E-owned lots near Ramona, Lois, and Dona Avenues

cupertino.title: Cupertino City Council — October 6, 2026
cupertino.summary: The Cupertino City Council's agenda for October 6, 2026 includes closed-session items on potential litigation and real property negotiations for 10480 Finch Avenue, along with routine consent items like meeting minutes and treasurer's reports. The agenda also lists approval of a property exchange agreement for the Finch property, a public information session on soil contamination remediation at The Rise, and a TEFRA public hearing for conduit financing related to The RISE.
keyTopics: Closed session on anticipated litigation and real property negotiations for 10480 Finch Avenue with Cupertino Union School District
Approval of an Exchange Agreement for the Finch Property at a negotiated purchase price of $11.8 million
Resolution increasing employer contributions for retiree medical/hospitalization insurance under PEMHCA for pre-August 2004 hires
Resolution authorizing an $80,000 grant application for the Rubberized Pavement Grant Program
Public information session on the approved remediation plan for soil contamination at The Rise, plus a TEFRA public hearing on conduit financing for the project

santa-clara.title: Santa Clara City Council and Authorities Concurrent — October 6, 2026
santa-clara.summary: The October 6 Santa Clara City Council and Authorities Concurrent agenda includes a report on pedestrian access restrictions on Lawrence and San Tomas Expressways and a staff presentation on data center policy, including water use and grid support. It also lists requests for future discussion of data center power allocation, a possible moratorium and non-disclosure agreements, along with Stadium Authority finances and parking concerns near apartments and stadium events.
keyTopics: Report and potential Council action on pedestrian access restrictions on portions of Lawrence and San Tomas Expressways
Staff presentation on updating city policies for new data center development, covering water usage and grid support participation

Council requests for future discussion of data center entitlement and power allocation, a possible moratorium on standalone data centers, and a proposed prohibition on non-disclosure agreements with standalone data centers
Stadium Authority financial status report for the quarter ending June 30, 2026 and related budget amendments
Deferred council requests on resident parking near apartment complexes, compensation for vehicles ticketed/towed during stadium events, and parking requirements for affordable housing projects

milpitas.title: Milpitas City Council — September 15, 2026
milpitas.summary: The Milpitas City Council agenda for September 15, 2026 listed items on federal housing and community development funding, red light traffic cameras, and the condition of the Milpitas Community Center. It also included finance-related items tied to the city's former redevelopment agency, including bond refunding.
keyTopics: Draft Program Year 2025 Community Development Block Grant Consolidated Plan
Presentation on the Red Light Camera Traffic Safety Program
Presentation on the condition of the Milpitas Community Center
Resolution for the Successor Agency to the Redevelopment Agency
Resolution for the sale and issuance of refunding bonds for the Successor Agency

palo-alto.title: Palo Alto Climate Action and Sustainability Committee — October 2, 2026
palo-alto.summary: The Palo Alto Climate Action and Sustainability Committee's agenda for October 2, 2026 included staff and committee member comments, plus an update on the city's electric system long-duration resiliency efforts. A late-added staff presentation on this item noted that it has been determined not to be a project under CEQA.
keyTopics: Update on Electric System Long Duration Resiliency
CEQA determination of 'Not a Project' for the resiliency item, with an added staff presentation
